title: Encoding ancient Greek musical notation
text:
Ancient Greek music used two parallel systems of notation: one vocalic, one instrumental
Unicode’s representation of these notes is ambiguous: graphically identical vocal and instrumental code points not distinguished
We follow the encoding of Greek musical notation defined in the Holy Cross undergraduate thesis of Zach Sowerby (HC ’19) using URNs to identify musical notation

title: Encoding ancient Greek musical notation
text:
Sowerby URN notation

All URNs are in the namespace urn:cite2:zst: (assumed in short forms used in this package)
There are two collections: gvn (vocal) and gin (instrumental)
Notes (object identifiers) have up to five dot-separated tiers of note citation :

base note
sharpenings of the base note
length value: diseme, triseme, tetraseme, and pentaseme
arsis dot (stigme): 1 indicates arsis, or the lack of metrical emphasis (in comparison to thesis, or metrical emphasis)
hyphen: when present (1) indicates multiple notes sounded over a single syllable

title: Encoding ancient Greek musical notation
text:
Realizing notes in Unicode
The first two dotted values (base note and its sharpenings) together can be mapped to Unicode code points. This table their possible values.1
Examples of finding Unicode code points: gvn:1.1 (vocal E) and gvn:1.2. (vocal first sharp of E). Both are in vocal notation collection (gvn); both refer to same base pitch (gvn:1); the second tier distinguishes E (gvn:1.1, mapped to 𝈀) from the first sharp of E (gvn:1.2, mapped to 𝈁).
Full examples: gvn:11.1.1.0.0 encodes a note in Greek vocal notation (gvn collection). It identifies the first sharp of note 11 (gvn:11.1), vocal a, with Unicode visualization Ϲ. Its length value is 1 (gvn:11.1.1), implying no additional diseme, triseme, tetraseme, or pentaseme. It has no arsis or hyphen the last two pieces of (gvn:11.1.1.0.0).

title: Basic parsing
text:
from mousike import syllabify, parse_notes
from mousike.align import read_cex

# 1) Read both editions: dict of passage reference -> content
texts = read_cex("data/seikilos_text.cex")
notation = read_cex("data/seikilos_notation.cex")

for ref, text in texts.items():
    # 2) Syllables for this passage (syllabify gives a list per word; flatten it)
    syllables = [s for word in syllabify(text) for s in word]

    # 3) Notes for this passage, as Note objects
    notes = parse_notes(notation[ref])

    print(ref, syllables)
    print(ref, [n.unicode for n in notes])

title: The Note object
text: Everything you can do with a Note, using as an example gvn:14.1.3.1.1.

title: The Note object
text:
Constructor

Note("gvn:14.1.3.1.1") makes a note from a short URN.
Note("urn:cite2:zst:gvn:14.1.3.1.1") makes the same note from the full URN.
Note("gvn:14.1") works too. The missing values default to length 1, no arsis and no hyphen.
Note("gcn:1") makes the rest. Its sharpening is None.
An invalid URN raises ValueError. That covers a pitch not in the table, a length outside 1–5, an arsis or hyphen value other than 0 or 1, and badly formed URNs.

title: The Note object
text:
Properties of a Note

n.collection gives 'gvn'.
n.base gives 14.
n.sharpening gives 1, meaning no sharp. 2 is the first sharp and 3 the second.
n.length gives 3. 1 means no length sign; 2 to 5 are diseme, triseme, tetraseme and pentaseme.
n.arsis gives True.
n.hyphen gives True.
n.unicode gives 'Ι', the written symbol. It depends only on the pitch.
n.name gives "vocal d′".

title: The Note object
text:
Identity

n.urn gives 'gvn:14.1.3.1.1'. It always includes all five values.
n.full_urn gives 'urn:cite2:zst:gvn:14.1.3.1.1'.
str(n) gives the same as n.urn.
repr(n) gives Note('gvn:14.1.3.1.1').

title: The Note object
text:
Vocal or instrumental

n.vocal gives True.
n.instrumental gives False.

title: The Note object
text:
Comparison

== compares all six values, so Note("gvn:11.1") == Note("gvn:11.1.1.0.0") is True.
Notes can go in sets and be dictionary keys.
Notes can’t be changed after creation; assigning to an attribute raises AttributeError.

title: The Note object
text:
Working with lists of notes

parse_notes(s) turns a notation-edition string into a flat list of Note objects.
parse_note_groups(s) gives one list per syllable, with notes joined by ~ kept together.
groups_to_unicode(groups) turns those groups back into a Unicode string, with spaces between groups.
In an alignment, each syllable’s note_group holds its Note objects.
